newsitem.title: USA: Semiconductor equipment Dec book-to-bill ratio up.
newsitem.headline: Semiconductor equipment Dec book-to-bill ratio up.

text.p: The North American semiconductor equipment book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.02 in December from 0.90 in November, reflecting improving orders for the chipmaking industry, a trade group reported Thursday.

The closely watched ratio measures the health of companies that supply chipmakers with manufacturing equipment. A book-to-bill ratio of 1.02 means $102 in orders were received by the equipment makers in December for each $100 worth of product shipped.

Semiconductor equipment stocks rose moderately Friday on the news. Shares of Applied Materials Inc, the biggest vendor, rose 1/2 to 45-5/8 in early afternoon Nasdaq trading. KLA Instruments Corp jumped 1-1/8 to 41. And Novellus Systems Inc rose 1/2 to 67.

Total semiconductor orders in December rose 11 percent to $1.04 billion in December from the prior month, said Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International, the industry's main trade group. It was the first month since June that monthly bookings topped $1 billion.
December 1996 bookings were 19.5 percent below the same month in 1995, the group said.
